title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
description:
# Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array

You are given an integer array `nums` sorted in **non-decreasing order**. Remove the duplicates **in-place** so that each distinct value appears exactly once in the front of the array, preserving the original relative order.

Return the number of distinct values, called `k`.

The judge checks two things:

*   The returned value is `k`.
*   The first `k` elements of `nums` are exactly the distinct values from the original array, in order.

Values after index `k - 1` do not matter.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,1,2]
**Output:** 2, nums = [1,2,_]
**Explanation:** There are two distinct values. The method must return `2`, and the first two positions of `nums` must be `1` and `2`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [0,0,1,1,1,2,2,3,3,4]
**Output:** 5, nums = [0,1,2,3,4,_,_,_,_,_]
**Explanation:** The compacted prefix contains the five distinct values in the same order.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4`
*   `-100 <= nums[i] <= 100`
*   `nums` is sorted in **non-decreasing** order.

tests.description: Lower value boundary with repeated runs

Both constraint boundaries and repeated interior values

solutions.name: Write Pointer with Last Kept Value
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep `write` as the length of the compacted unique prefix. Scan every value from left to right. A value is copied into `nums[write]` only when the prefix is empty or the value differs from the last value already kept.

## Key Insight

The array is sorted, so all copies of the same value are adjacent. Once the last kept value differs from the current value, this current value is the first occurrence of a new run and belongs at the next write position.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Run-Length Group Compression
solutions.description:
## Approach

Treat the sorted array as runs of equal values. At the start of each run, write that value once into the compacted prefix, then advance the read pointer across the rest of the run.

## Key Insight

This is the run-length encoding view of the problem. Sorting turns duplicate removal into taking exactly one representative from each consecutive run.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Binary Search Next Run Boundary
solutions.description:
## Approach

Because the array is sorted, use binary search to jump from the first value of a run to the first value greater than it. Write one representative per run into the prefix.

## Key Insight

The linear run-length method advances through duplicates one by one. Binary search teaches the same sorted-run boundary idea from a different angle: each step asks for the upper bound of the current value.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(k log n), where `k` is the number of distinct values
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Quadratic Shift Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan adjacent values. When a duplicate is found, shift every later element one position left and shrink the active length. Keep checking the same index because another duplicate may have shifted into it.

## Key Insight

This baseline directly performs deletion from an array. It is inefficient, but it makes the write-pointer optimization concrete: instead of repeatedly shifting the suffix, the optimized solution writes each distinct value once.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
